name: IL-13
label: Safe D

key_factors: Budzinski holds a massive financial advantage, with $2.6 million on hand versus Wilson's $12,000
The district leans Democratic by about five points and the national environment favors Democrats
Prediction markets price Budzinski at roughly 96% to win
No public general-election polling is available, leaving the forecast dependent on fundamentals
model.rationale: Every available signal points the same way: a Democratic-leaning seat, a well-funded incumbent, a challenger with almost no cash, and markets pricing this as a near-certain Democratic hold. The forecast stays close to the fundamentals-based estimate, trimmed slightly for the absence of polling.
model.watch: Any late surge of outside Republican spending or a sharp deterioration in the national environment for Democrats would be the main things to watch.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
First-term incumbent Nikki Budzinski defends a central Illinois district that leans Democratic by about five points. She enters the general election with a commanding financial position, having raised nearly $2.9 million and holding $2.6 million on hand, while Republican Jeff Wilson has raised under $350,000 and reports only about $12,000 in cash. Outside spending has so far been minimal and one-sided.

No public general-election polls are available and no expert raters have listed the race, so the outlook rests on fundamentals, money, and prediction markets, which price Budzinski at roughly 96 percent. With the incumbent renominated unopposed for her party's nomination and the challenger lacking resources, this race ranks among the safest Democratic holds of the cycle.
